item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Fighting has resumed in the Kherson region after the longest ceasefire ended, with Russian strikes killing at least 26 people. Russian drones have been fitted with makeshift armor of nets and rubber tires and are being deployed as decoys for one-way attacks up to 1,200 km, while both Ukrainian hackers and Russian actors have compromised emergency alert apps to issue fake nuclear warnings. A Russian Su‑57 fighter was destroyed by an engine fire at Akhtubinsk airfield, and Russian troops have used the Oleshky ceasefire to mask movements. Russia launched its biggest mass attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure this year, and 75,767 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Uganda is accelerating its pullout of African Union peacekeeping troops from Somalia, targeting a 2027 exit, while Ethiopia also plans to withdraw its forces as fighting intensifies at home. The United States and an East African nation have begun joint airstrikes against an al-Qaeda-linked group, and the UAE carried out its first drone strike against al-Shabaab in nearly a year. Puntland mercenaries are fighting alongside Sudanese RSF forces, and the Sudanese army reports northern Somali fighters supporting the RSF. Armed terrorists are reported crossing the Kaduna River toward Shiroro in Niger State, indicating a new movement of fighters. Journalists continue to face impunity, with 12 of 13 killed since 2006 still without justice. The conflict also sees ongoing kidnappings of Islamic school students and a dynamite explosion linked to smugglers moving explosives to Burkina Faso. item.title: Nigeria: the situation
item.description:
Gunmen continue abducting civilians and attacking security forces across northern Nigeria, including the kidnapping of a university student in Plateau, the abduction of two visually impaired persons in Plateau, and the seizure of 14 schoolchildren from a farm. Security operatives have rescued multiple victims, such as eight abducted residents in Kaduna, a pregnant woman and seven others in Kaduna, and a group of 37 worshippers held for 212 days in Kaduna. Bandits have killed vigilantes and police officers, including a vigilante member in Plateau and five police officers in a Sokoto-Zamfara highway ambush. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
